scope: Actual queue task-table binding, task change dispatch, submitted task installation and ordered same-change batch execution used by Coordinator::apply. Complete mixed-event dispatch/replay, reader retirement and native WAL/lock binding remain open.

properties.identity/task_id: Exact borrowed task identity extraction and missing/type error classification.
properties.dispatch/edit: Same selected queue task receives the supplied retry, lease, failure, terminal or progress update; all unrelated root fields and peer tasks are preserved. Missing target and local task errors leave the queue unchanged.
properties.submit: Install the exact six-field pending task under spec.task_id with supplied order; preserve other roots and peer tasks; precise identity/target errors without mutation.
properties.edit_many: Ordered arbitrary finite supplied IDs, including duplicates, receive the same specified change. Success completes the trace; failure describes the exact completed prefix and first failing ID with no subsequent edits.
properties.trace_frame: Induction over the successful trace preserves every non-task root field and every task not selected in the supplied ID prefix.

runtime_changes: Coordinator delegates queue task selection and epoch retry batches to the verified source. Borrowed String identities and mutable field lookup avoid extra key allocation; no new I/O or persisted format. No newly demonstrated valid-API bug or measured zero-overhead claim.
boundaries: Existing twenty audited serde primitives and String ordering/content assumptions remain; no new primitive, opaque type, Value law or admitted straw body.
Batch traces apply one uniform supplied Change. They are not the complete mixed-event Coordinator fold.

Outer event type/argument selection, epoch assignment, global scheduling order allocation, cache maintenance, compound reader/receipt effects, request admission and quarantine remain caller obligations.
Reader retirement retain/callback refinement, full root extraction and native WAL/File/run/lock binding and cross-log/GC composition are unfinished.
